simple.meaning: נָכֶה (nâkeh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “smitten , i.e. (literally) maimed, or (figuratively) dejected.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 2 Samuel 4:4. The surrounding context includes family line, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָכֶה (H5223) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: נָכֶה (nâkeh) / H5223 is traced through 2 Samuel 4:4, 2 Samuel 9:3, Isaiah 66:2 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Now Jonathan, Saul’s son, had a son who was lame in his feet. He was five years old when the news came about Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel; and his nurse picked him up and fled. As she hurried to flee, he fell and became lame. His name was Mephibosheth.
